page.layout: Full-width title "Index rerum." under a decorative rule; below it two columns. Left column: letter A and its entries. Right column: letter B and its entries, then letter C and its entries. No margin notes, no page number.

main_text.head: Index rerum.
main_text.l: ADoptio dignitatem bonorum operum facit, cap. 20. § 13.
Æqualitas Justitia ad præmium vitæ æternæ falsò tribuitur operibus, cap. 5. §. 1. &c. Vid. Justitia.
Ambulare in via ad Regnum cœleste, quid, cap. 20. §. 8. Probat necessitatem eperandi absque merito, ibid.
Judicium ejus vindicatur contra virtutem nostram merendi, tanquam ex meritis Christi, cap. 17. sect. 11, & 12, &c.
BEneficia maxima quæ in nescientes nolentésque conferuntur, cap. 16. sect. 5.
Bonorum operum imperfectio ex Patribus, cap. 2. § 9, & 11. Quomodo consistat cum bonitate operis, ut non illud censeatur peccatum, cap. 20. § 8, 9, 10.

CHristi Merita propria extrudi per Pontificiorum virtutem merendi, cap. 17. § 6. Talem virtutem negare, non est Christi meritis detrahere, § 7. Imò est gloriam Gratia amplificare, § 8, & 9. Dogma illud à Patribus proferuntur[?], § 10. Et est Romana Ecclesia veteris doctrina.

page.notes: The initials A, B and C are large letters joined to the first word of their entries (ADoptio, BEneficia, CHristi). The faint "Index rerum." above the rule is show-through from the reverse side and is left out. The word "proferuntur" is doubtful: the scan is blurred there. Some Greek and italic words are small; the Greek line "Ἀξίωσις" is transcribed as seen. The text in the final line is set right-aligned.
